title: Anyone using simple AI scripts to spot meal prep trends?
author: Savings-Theory-5661
selftext: I work long kitchen shifts and meal prep is the only thing keeping me on track. Last month I started feeding my grocery receipts and store flyers into a basic script that tracks weekly prices. Nothing fancy, just text parsing that flags when staples drop below my average. It caught a two week dip on chicken thighs I would've missed completely. Now I'm wondering if anyone here has tried something similar with restaurant waste data or produce markdown schedules. My script struggles with handwritten supplier notes, so tips on handling those would help.

comments.author: Murder_1337
comments.body: Sounds like you need to implement the new tech Jev works as a decision making layer prior to the LLM so it makes analyze data input and categorizes it and then you can feed that data to LLM. Basically because you’re sorting a bunch of data jev can really help with this, save tokens in LLM analyzing all the data and increase accuracy.
